title: Container sidecar dies silently on firewall-init failure (dnsmasq port 53): no surfacing, no respawn
description: Container mode. cam run spawns the sidecar (background supervisor, the sole driver of plan/implement/review/ship and the meta_loop=auto driver). At boot the sidecar runs the container firewall init (dnsmasq on port 53). Observed 2026-07-06 20:36: init failed with 'dnsmasq: failed to create listening socket for port 53: Address already in use' (a stale cam-worker container from an earlier session held port 53), the sidecar logged '[cam] container firewall init failed - no worker will be dispatched' and EXITED, becoming a zombie. Three compounding gaps: (1) no surfacing: the failure only lands in .claude/cam-supervisor.log; the orchestrator boot reads no marker (unlike .cam-ship-stalled.json / .cam-plan-escalated.json), so a subsequent cam plan / meta-loop phase:planning signal is written and silently never consumed (cam plan liveness gate checks the orchestrator pane, not the sidecar pid, so it exits 0 into a hang). (2) no respawn: nothing restarts a dead sidecar - only cam run-creates-session spawns it, and orch-recycle-watch only watches the orchestrator. Recovery today requires a full operator ceremony (cam stop + docker rm -f cam-worker + cam run). (3) no fail-safe on the collision: firewall init does not detect/reap a stale cam-worker container (or an existing dnsmasq) holding port 53 before binding, so a leftover container from a prior session hard-wedges the next session. Durable fixes: sidecar writes a durable escalation marker on firewall-init failure that the orchestrator surfaces at boot (mirror the ship-stalled/plan-escalated pattern); a sidecar-liveness watcher (parallel to orch-recycle-watch) that respawns or surfaces a dead sidecar; and firewall init that reaps a stale container/dnsmasq on the port-53 collision and retries fail-closed. Ties CAM-192 (image staleness), CAM-201 (container/CI parity + preflight fail-closed), CAM-180 (rebuild ceremony).
